concepts.def: A named location in memory that stores a value which can be read and changed while the program runs.
The kind of value a variable holds, such as integer, real, Boolean or string, which determines what operations are allowed on it.
A construct, such as if-elif-else, that chooses which statements to execute depending on whether a condition is true or false.
Repeating statements, either a set number of times with a for loop or while a condition remains true with a while loop.
A named block of code, a function or procedure, that performs a task and can be called whenever needed, avoiding repeated code.
A value passed into a subprogram when it is called, allowing the same code to work with different data each time.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Problem Solving With Programming — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Problem Solving With Programming brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Problem Solving With Programming.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A variable is best described as:
options: A named memory location whose stored value can change as the program runs
A fixed number that can never change
A type of loop
An error in the code

mcqs.q: Which construct executes different statements depending on a condition?
options: Selection (if/else)
Sequence
Declaration
Commenting

mcqs.q: A for loop is most appropriate when:
options: The number of repetitions is known in advance
The program should never repeat anything
You want the code to run only if a condition is false
You need to store text

mcqs.q: What distinguishes a function from a procedure?
options: A function returns a value to the code that called it
A function cannot take parameters
A procedure runs faster than any function
There is no difference at all

mcqs.q: In programming, does x = 5 ask whether x equals 5?
options: Yes - the equals sign always tests equality like in maths.
Yes - x = 5 deletes the variable x.
No - in most languages a single = is assignment, storing 5 in x; comparison uses a different operator such as ==.
Yes - while loops always run at least 10 times.

mcqs.q: Can a variable hold several values at the same time?
options: Yes - x = 5 deletes the variable x.
Yes - variables store one value per letter of their name.
No - a simple variable holds exactly one value; assigning a new value overwrites the old one. Storing many values needs a structure such as a list or array.
Yes - a variable remembers every value it has ever been given.

mcqs.q: Does a loop with the condition WHILE x < 10 always run exactly 10 times?
options: Yes - while loops always run at least 10 times.
No - how many times it runs depends on x's starting value and how x changes inside the loop; it may run zero times or forever.
Yes - the number in the condition is the number of repetitions.
Yes - x = 5 deletes the variable x.
